Subject: Re: 503/429 surge this morning — user-facing timeouts

Joining bridge — joined. Initial findings (5:30 into triage):
- Traffic pattern: a ~3x burst from Finella's IP ranges starting 08:44 PST. Many of these requests had identical prompt prefixes and caused repeated KV-cache misses.
- Autoscaler: a recent config change (rolled on 2026-11-12) lowered the scale-up aggressiveness to reduce cost; it now takes ~75s to provision additional worker capacity. That combined with the burst caused queue saturation.
- Client retries: Finella's client retries were aggressive (5 immediate retries) and compounded the burst into a retry storm.
- Worker errors: a minority of workers started returning 500s due to OOMs while processing the large batch sizes.

Mitigation completed at 09:10 PST:
- Disabled aggressive autoscaler cap (rolled back to previous policy).
- Increased per-customer concurrency quota for Finella by +30% for the next 6 hours.
- Applied a temporary gateway soft-rate-limit for high-frequency requests from Finella IPs (503 -> 429 fold-down).

Outcome: error rate dropped to baseline (~0.6%) by 09:38 PST. We kept the bridge open for monitoring.

Next steps (short):
1) Capture the full GC and OOM logs for the affected workers and attach to the incident.
2) Add a specific alert for sustained KV-cache miss rate + queue latency correlation (alerts currently only track queue length).
3) Draft a customer-facing incident summary + executive note.

Jonas: can you validate whether the autoscaler rollback is safe across other tenants?

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem draft + proposed action items (please review)

Team — attaching the first draft of the postmortem and a compressed set of action items. The QA pass is still pending but I wanted to get these in front of you before Monday's leadership sync. Key points below, doc attached: postmortem-fnella-draft.md

Executive summary (one para):
On 2026-11-13 at ~08:45 PST Finella experienced an elevated 5xx/429 error wave driven by a burst of similar requests that triggered repeated KV-cache misses and compounded with aggressive client retries. A recent change to the autoscaler reduced scale-up aggressiveness, increasing time-to-scale and allowing queue saturation. Mitigations (autoscaler rollback, soft gateway rate-limit, temporary capacity bump) restored baseline within ~50 minutes. Root cause: combination of autoscaler tuning + client retry behavior + workload-specific cache pressure.

Proposed technical actions (owners, ETA):
- Alerting: create composite alert that fires on (KV-cache miss rate > 15% for 2m) AND (queue latency P95 > 250ms) -> owner: Rishi, ETA: 2d.
- Runbook: add a 'retry-storm' playbook with explicit steps (apply soft-rate-limit, emergency capacity bump, check autoscaler config, isolate tenant) -> owner: Dev, ETA: 3d. Attach: runbook-retries-v2.md.
- Autoscaler: revert the cost-driven aggressiveness change and add a safe-guard flag per-tenant to avoid under-scaling -> owner: Jonas, ETA: 1w.
- Client guidance: collaborate with Finella SDK team to recommend exponential backoff and jitter; publish guidance in customer portal -> owner: Hannah, ETA: 5d.
- SLO tuning: evaluate whether the P95 SLO for gateway should account for tail retries; short term: add a temporary SLO slack window for Finella while we finish mitigations -> owner: Product (cc: Marissa), ETA: 2d.

Risks & follow-ups:
- A rollback of cost measures will increase short-term infra spend. Finance and sales (Marissa) to lead the customer credit discussion if required.
- Need a canary around autoscaler change to prevent across-tenant regressions.

Please review the attached draft and reply with edits. I will push a cleaned version to Drive and to HubSpot (DEAL-1923) once we've agreed.

Attachments: postmortem-fnella-draft.md, grafana-5xx-spike.png

— Dev
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
